Welcome toGrange Primary School
Our school is a home of great learning and progress. Each day we aim to build the Confidence and Consideration levels of each child through the power of education. We call this the CC WAY. We are a school that believes in Inclusion and we believe that Kindness is strength; Diversity is Wealth and that true strength is strength of Character. We strive to make the difference in children’s lives by helping each and every one of our children make strong progress in their learning and helping them to develop powerful positive habits of learning and deep reservoirs of knowledge.
We hope that you enjoy looking around our website and getting a feel for our school.
Mr Daniel KerbelHeadteacher

Thank you for being an inspiration. Your classroom is a place of growth, respect and learning, and we are grateful that our child has been a part of it.

Headteacher's Welcome
Dear Grange Community and Visitors,
This is my eighth year as Headteacher of Grange and it feels very special. The children who started in Nursery when I first arrived will now graduate at the end of this school year, and I look forward to celebrating their journey with you.
Grange is a kind and welcoming school. Children often tell us that they feel safe and at home here, even when they join us later in their school years.
Our vision is simple but powerful: it is not only about who we are right now, but about who we can become:
We see every child as the hope for tomorrow, and we treat them accordingly. We believe true strength is character strength: learning from mistakes, reflecting, and growing.
At Grange we follow restorative practice. Mistakes are not failures – they are learning opportunities that help us build resilience and wisdom. Good behaviour is not just expected; it is an attitude and collective responsibility that we all strive towards as we learn and grow together.
We call this our Grange CC Way – balancing Confidence with Consideration.
In this way, our children learn to value themselves and to make the world better through their thoughts, words, actions, and choices.
Above all, we encourage everyone to aim for their PB – Personal Best. Competitions with others may happen, but what matters most is not how we compare with them, but how we strive to challenge ourselves in order to become the very best version of who we can be.
We welcome you to Grange for who you are, and for the goodness, progress and learning you bring to our community.
I feel proud and grateful to be part of this wonderful school, and I look forward to meeting you as you too become part of our Grange family.

pageCache.text:
Shakespeare Project
Each year our Year 5 pupils take part in the Primary Shakespeare Company's project in the Summer Term.
A different Shakespeare play is chosen every year and each class is responsible for one Act of the play. The Company send theatre practitioners into Grange to work with the pupils on their performance over the course of one half term and the project ends with a Festival Day where everyone performs their Act alongside other participating schools.
Learning across all subjects, including Home Learning, is linked to the chosen play for the year to fully immerse our pupils in their learning and it is always a great success - a good reminder to us all that William Shakespeare's work is accessible for anyone!

pageCache.text:
2024-2025
Primary Shakespeare Company Prize-Giving 2024 at the House of Lords
In the Summer Term, we were lucky enough to win the Primary Shakespeare Company's Annie Williams Prize for all of our hard work on the musical 'Calpurnia'. This is a prize that is awarded to the school that shows the children's outstanding immersion in the play and curriculum, demonstrating impact through attainment and the wider school community as well as the classes. Winning this prize is truly a testament to ALL of the Year 5 children's hard work and we could not be prouder.
We were invited to a prize-giving ceremony at the House of Lords this week to receive our trophy. Ainara and Naomi represented Grange to share their thoughts about their own experience through the project which left the company's founders extremely impressed. We also met Estelle Morris - a current member of the House of Lords and previous Secretary of State for Education and Skills - who thoroughly enjoyed conversing with Ainara and Naomi about their experience.
Well done and congratulations to Klee Class and Matisse Class!

2025-2026
Primary Shakespeare Company Prize-Giving 2025 at the House Of Lords
For the second time in a row, we were lucky enough to win the Primary Shakespeare Company's Annie Williams Prize thanks to the hard work of last year's Year 5 children and staff. This is a prize that is awarded to the school that shows the children's outstanding immersion in the play and curriculum, demonstrating impact through attainment and the wider school community as well as the classes.
We could not be prouder of everyone's efforts and we are very grateful to be included in such a brilliant project year on year. On Thursday 18th September, we took two (now) Year 6 pupils to the House of Lords to help us do a presentation about the work completed in the Summer Term last academic year. Izan and Matei shared their thoughts about their own experience through the project which left the company's founders extremely impressed - they really did shine.
The prize-giving was such an inspiring afternoon and a brilliant celebration of the arts, music, creativity, collaboration and the power of Shakespeare for all children. It was wonderful to see other Harrow schools proudly representing the borough too.
Well done and congratulations to Malala Class and Rumi Class!

pageCache.text:
Reading
At Grange, we believe reading underpins all aspects of learning. We aim to encourage children to foster a love of reading and a curiosity to learn more, ultimately developing proficient communicators and readers equipped for their future. We inspire a love of reading in various ways:
Every child from Year 1 onwards takes part in guided reading lessons daily. At Grange, we use an holistic, talk based approach to reading alongside the direct teaching of reading skills through VIPERS questioning and long-term teaching of specific objectives. Regular reading and discussion of the text read are vital in developing children’s decoding, reading and comprehension skills. Children work together to read and understand texts appropriate for their reading attainment.
Each year group focuses on a different text every half term; our choices of literature aim to engage the children, enrich their understanding of the world they live in and empower them to grow as people and learners.
Studies show that reading for pleasure makes a big difference to children’s educational performance. Evidence suggests that children who read for enjoyment every day not only perform better in reading tests than those who don’t, but also develop a broader vocabulary, increased general knowledge and a better understanding of other cultures.
At Grange, we encourage a reading for pleasure ethos through daily reading sessions called ‘DEAR’ time (‘Drop Everything And Read’), class story time, reading challenges and reading events such as World Book Day. All children have independent access to a wide variety of high-quality texts in their classroom reading areas and the school library. High-quality texts are also used in all aspects of teaching across the curriculum and provide children with the opportunities to extend and enrich their learning.
Every child is expected to read with an adult at home for 15 minutes every day. Teachers provide children with books from the classroom that are matched to their reading level. We encourage parents to be actively engaged in order to support children’s ongoing learning and development; sharing enthusiasm and enjoyment of reading will promote positive attitudes to learning.
Each class also has a scheduled weekly slot to visit the library where they can peruse at their leisure and choose a book to borrow and take home in addition to the books provided by their class teacher.

Grange Explorers - Adventure books
Grange Explorers: A New Adventure in Learning!
We are excited to introduce a brand-new enrichment initiative for the 2025–26 academic year:Grange Explorers – Adventure BooksThis is a fun and inspiring way to encourage all children to go beyond the classroom and explore the world around them while building new skills and experiences.
Each child has received an Adventure Booklet filled with 20–30 exciting challenges linked to their year group’s curriculum. These include creative activities, outdoor learning, community experiences, and tasks designed to build confidence, curiosity, and independence.
- Children complete tasks at home, in school or on trips with their family over the school year.- They collect stamps from their teacher as they complete each one.- They must show their teacher some evidence of what they have completed at home - this could be emailed to the year group email address, uploaded to google classroom or brought in to school- There’s no pressure to complete them all – it’s about enjoying the journey and trying new things!- Children who do complete all the tasks by the end of the school year will receive a special reward
✅ Building character and independence✅ Strengthening curriculum links beyond the classroom✅ Promoting outdoor learning and community engagement✅ Supporting British values, creativity, and well-being
- Encouraging them to try a task each week or month- Celebrating their efforts with them- Getting involved with activities that interest them
We’re looking forward to seeing all the wonderful adventures our pupils go on this year. Thank you for your continued support in helping your child flourish and grow.

pageCache.pageTitle: Spanish (Modern Foreign Languages) - Grange Primary School
pageCache.text:
Spanish (Modern Foreign Languages)
With approximately 470 million people speaking Spanish as a native language and it being the official language of 21 countries, we have chosen Spanish to be the Modern Foreign Language taught at Grange. In fact, Spanish is second only to Mandarin in terms of its number of native speakers worldwide.
At Grange, Spanish is taught from Year 3 onwards by a specialist teacher in our Languages Classroom. We follow the guidance in the National Curriculum programme of study for Languages which suggests that children should make substantial progress in one language through four years of study in Key Stage 2. The curriculum focuses on pupils developing their vocabulary, phonics and grammar knowledge and it has been designed in a way that enables pupils to revisit their prior learning frequently through retrieval activities.
We believe that language learning helps children to develop creativity, problem solving skills and supports oracy and literacy in English. Language learning also promotes children’s intercultural understanding and appreciation of the rest of the world. There are plenty of opportunities for pupils to learn about the culture of Spanish speaking countries such as Mexico, Guatemala, Colombia and Peru.
Spanish lessons are interactive and practical; children learn the language through games, songs and stories. Initially, the focus is on developing speaking and listening skills as well as transferable language learning strategies. Our pupils are also given access to, and taught how to use, bilingual dictionaries. In years 5 and 6, children have opportunities to develop their reading and writing skills further.
Links are made to other areas of the curriculum such as English, Maths and Science. For example, we compare English and Spanish grammar rules and children learn to tell the time in Spanish and how to describe the Solar System.
We have developed opportunities for children to consolidate their Spanish learning outside of their weekly Spanish lessons. For example, across KS2, the children answer the attendance and lunch registers in Spanish daily. We also have a few enrichment activities planned throughout the year to enhance pupils’ experience. These include Spanish film events provided by the British Film Institute, Spanish storytelling sessions provided by Freshwater Theatre Company and Flamenco dance workshops.
Through Spanish lessons, we hope to engender a lifelong love of language and cultural learning as well as ensuring our pupils are ‘secondary ready’ and prepared for life in a globalised world.

New Page
Young Ambassadors for Peace – Spreading Peace, Kindness and Harmony at Grange
On Wednesday 23rd September, our newly appointed Young Ambassadors for Peace (YAP) visited the Brahma Kumaris World Spiritual University for a special day of Peace Education, marking the United Nations International Day of Peace.
The visit was a wonderful opportunity for our ambassadors to begin exploring what it means to promote peace, kindness, respect and harmony within our school and the wider world.
Peace Begins Within Us
Throughout the day, the children explored the idea of “Peace Within the Self” and considered an important message: creating a more peaceful world begins with developing peace within ourselves.
They reflected on how our thoughts, words and actions can affect others and discovered that peace is not simply about avoiding conflict. Peace can be shown through kindness, helping others, listening, showing respect, understanding one another and finding positive ways to solve disagreements.
Our Young Ambassadors shared some thoughtful reflections about what they had learned:
Neeyam: “I have learned about making peace and harmony throughout the world.”
Hadi: “I’ve learned that you can make peace and be friendly. Conflict can end and there won’t be disagreements.”
Fatema: “Each time you help, things get better and there is more peace.”
Ranuthi: “It is all about kindness, helping others and showing them respect.”
Sophia: “Peace is happiness.”
Partiv: “I’ve learned that making the world better is right for our world.”
Finding Peace in the World Around UsThe children also took part in a one-minute peaceful moment outdoors, quietly observing and appreciating nature. This gave them an opportunity to slow down, notice their surroundings and think about how peaceful moments can support our wellbeing.
Our ambassadors also explored peace through art. They looked carefully at different paintings and discussed which images made them feel most peaceful. They considered how colour, shape and imagery can communicate feelings of peace without using any words.
Through their Peace Gym activities, the children continued to develop their understanding of calmness, friendship, kindness and peaceful problem-solving.
The day gave our Young Ambassadors time to reflect, discuss, listen and learn, while developing a deeper understanding of their important new role.
They returned to Grange with ideas about how they can share their learning and encourage others to make positive choices. Throughout the year, our Young Ambassadors for Peace will continue to look for ways to promote kindness, respect, friendship, calmness and harmony across our school community.
This is only the beginning of their journey, and we look forward to seeing our Young Ambassadors share their learning and inspire others.
Small acts of kindness can make a big difference. Together, we can help peace grow at Grange and beyond.

Governors
Governing Board Attendance
Governors are expected to attend all meetings and contribute to moving the school forward.
The Role of a School Governor
School Governors are members of a school Governing Board. They have responsibility for raising school standards through three key roles - Setting Strategic Direction, ensuring accountability and monitoring & evaluating school performance. They are the largest volunteer force in the country. The Governing Board consist of parents, staff members, members of the community and appointed representatives from the Local Authority.
